artifacts.summary: Audits every git-commit-scoped.sh call site, empirically reproduces current behavior in scratch repos, finds the task's literal premise (all-drop -> exit 0) is already fixed by an existing V3 post-filter gate, identifies the real residual gap (partial drop + empty resulting commit, indistinguishable from benign no-op), and recommends a corrected option (c) over (a)/(b).

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh already refuses (exit 2) when 100% of positive pathspecs drop as unmatched (V3 post-filter gate, added in task 226 phase 2, commit 94256557d). The remaining false-success gap is narrower: a PARTIAL drop (one or more pathspecs unmatched) combined with the surviving matched pathspecs having zero actual working-tree diff produces the same exit 1 'nothing to commit' as the fully benign all-zero-drop case -- these two are indistinguishable at the exit-code level today. Any future fix must key off (drop_count > 0 AND commit produced nothing), not literally '100% dropped', since the literal framing is already handled.

Every caller of git-commit-scoped.sh in this codebase uses the idiom `bash .../git-commit-scoped.sh ... || echo "WARN: ...(non-blocking)"`. Because `A || B` evaluates to B's exit status in bash, ANY nonzero exit from the script (1, 2, 3, or a future new code) collapses to exit 0 for the calling script's own control flow. A louder/more distinguishing exit code added inside the script is necessary but NOT sufficient to prevent a repeat incident -- at least one caller must be changed to branch on $? explicitly and escalate, or the fix is correct-but-inert in practice.
